This spec waives its own test with `@no-test` and points at a scenario code as the proof elsewhere.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Judgment | an AI or a person answers the question below, through `anchors judge` |
| Confronts | `spec` |
| Blocking by default — new project | yes |
| Blocking by default — existing project | no — informs |

## The question

> This spec waives its own test with `@no-test` and points at a scenario code as the proof elsewhere. Find the test that mentions that code and answer: does it EXERCISE the behaviour this spec describes, or does it only cite the code? Fail it if the mention is in a comment, if the test exercises another behaviour, or if the proof is so indirect that a break in this unit would not bring it down. The question is about what the test RUNS, not about what its name promises.

## Declaring it

```yaml
gates:
  - name: no-test-proof-real
    on: [spec]
    measures: judgment
```
